Kate has practiced chess for three years and won a prize last term. Kate usually spends the weekend reading at the library. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Best of all, the new semester starts in September.
Kate believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. Little by little, things began to change. Grace always says that small steps matter more than big plans. Her housemates split the bills evenly.

At first, Kate found it difficult to keep the habit. On Friday evenings, Kate reviews the notes from class. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. The chancellor opened the science block.

The playground looked quieter than usual that evening. Kate wrote down every idea in a small notebook. Grace and Kate are preparing a report about the playground. Old fans love to bemoan the rising price of tickets.
There are always more possibilities than we expect. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on.
